data.long_meaning: Satyaasya is a name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Satya', which means 'truth' or 'reality'. In Hindu mythology, Satyaasya is a name given to several gods and goddesses representing truth and honesty. The name Satyaasya carries the meaning “Truth, Reality” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Satyaasya usually hope their child will grow to embody truth, reality and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Satyaasya total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

It is believed that speaking the truth is a fundamental virtue and it brings peace and harmony in society. The name reminds us of the importance of being truthful in our actions and words, which in turn leads to virtuous living. It also represents the idea of truth as a steady, unchanging entity that should be valued above all else.

historical_references.reference: The sage Satyasrama, also known as Satyaasya, is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. He is a descendant of the lunar dynasty and is a great sage and a dedicated yogi. During the great battle of Kurukshetra, he performs severe austerities to gain the blessings of Lord Shiva. As a reward, he receives the Pasupata weapon, which is a powerful and divine weapon capable of destroying all evil.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India, around the 4th century BCE

historical_references.reference: Another reference to the sage Satyasrama, also known as Satyaasya, can be found in the Puranas. According to some legends, he was granted the boon of immortality by Lord Shiva, making him an immortal sage.
